name: Kyōyū (共有)
summary: Code shared by the Kyoten Kūkō flight-simulation apps

changed: `style/tokens.css`: Kōhō's accent `--kk-kouhou` is violet `#6b4fc8` (was a provisional slate), chosen by the owner; white text on it stays.

The package is renamed `kyouyou` → `kyouyuu` (display name Kyōyū), and its repository `brianhvo02/kyouyou` → `brianhvo02/kyouyuu` (GitHub redirects the old address). Short names now write long vowels out as typed (`ou`, `uu`); display names carry macrons (Kyoten Kūkō, Kōro, Kōkūzu, Kansei, Kōhō, Kakunōko, Kyōyū), on the family bar's signs too (Kūkō, Kōro, Kakunōko).

`family-bar`: Kōkūzu's member id is `koukuuzu` (public address `https://koukuuzu.pages.dev/`, home path `../koukuuzu/`) and Kōhō's is `kouhou` (`https://kouhou.pages.dev/`, `../kouhou/`). `FAMILY` lists the new ids.
`project`: `ProjectId` adds `koukuuzu`, `kouhou` and `kyouyuu`; this package's own `project.json` now has the id `kyouyuu`.
`style/fonts.css`: the KK Mincho subset also carries 自動操縦, for Jidō Sōjū.

Deprecated, removed in the next release: the old ids `kokuzu` and `koho` in the family bar's `current` and `unavailable` (read as `koukuuzu` and `kouhou`); the tokens `--kk-kokuzu`, `--kk-on-kokuzu`, `--kk-koho`, `--kk-on-koho` and `data-kk-accent="kokuzu"` and `"koho"` (aliases of the new ones); and `kokuzu`, `koho` and `kyouyou` as `ProjectId`s.

To move an app: change the dependency to `"kyouyuu": "github:brianhvo02/kyouyuu#v0.20.0"` (and remove `kyouyou`), change imports `kyouyou/…` to `kyouyuu/…` (CSS `@import`s included), and switch the family-bar ids, tokens and `data-kk-accent` values above to the new names. The subpaths, exports and APIs are otherwise unchanged.

added: `project` and `family-bar`: Kōhō (航法) joins the family as `koho`, a `ProjectId` and a family-bar member between Kansei and Kakunouko (public address `https://koho.pages.dev/`, home path `../koho/`), with the accent tokens `--kk-koho` and `--kk-on-koho` (a provisional slate until Kōhō's page design) and `data-kk-accent="koho"`. Hosts upgrading should add `koho` to the family bar's `unavailable` until Kōhō is live, or the bar links an address with nothing behind it yet. The KK Mincho subset now carries 法.

`arinc424/records`: ARINC 424-18 record kinds: `recordKindName` names every common section and subsection, `recordLayout` gives the identity, sequence and continuation columns for twenty kinds (procedure legs, airspace, FIR/UIR, runways, airports, communications, MSAs, path points, airway restrictions, navaids, markers and GLS reference paths; one primary record per identity and sequence, except the communications kinds, marked `grouped`, whose records form a set), and `subsectionColumn` and `subsectionOf` find the subsection code (terminal NDBs included). Types: `RecordLayout`, `ColumnSpan`, `IdentityField`.
`arinc424/codes`: ARINC 424-18 codes in plain words: `describeAltitude`, `pathTerminatorName`, `routeTypeName`, `turnDirectionName` and `speedLimitDescription`.

`kansei-routes`: Kansei's helper lookups (airports, controllers, procedures, minimum sector altitudes) and plan saving as a transport-only Node request handler, built from data (`createKanseiRoutesFromData`) or from an X-Plane folder (`createKanseiRoutes`, which indexes in the background and answers 503 meanwhile). Also exports the file finders (`findAptFiles`, `findDataFile`, `findAtcFile`, `hasCifp`, `readCifpFrom`), `indexAptFiles`, `indexFixes`, `parseAtc` and the types (`Controller` among them), so a host, with or without an X-Plane folder, needs one import.

`wx/upstream`: `relayHazards` (with `hazardsUpstream` and `HAZARDS_PATH`), the weather-hazards relay: `?kind=sigmet|isigmet|gairmet` answers with NOAA's GeoJSON FeatureCollection, forwarding only the kind; callers cache it for 300 s.

`style/tokens.css`, `style/fonts.css`, `style/base.css`: the family style kit: `--kk-` tokens (palette, five accents, type, spacing, radii, focus ring, bar height) in light and dark, self-hosted B612, B612 Mono and a Noto Serif JP subset of the family's kanji, `data-kk-accent` for parts of a page in another member's accent, and opt-in base rules.

`family-bar`: `<kk-family-bar>`, the family's row of taxiway signs (the location sign for the current surface, direction signs to the others), with public and home link modes, unavailable members, and a compact or phone-width menu; registered by `defineFamilyBar()`.
`xplane/aptdat`: `readAptDat` streams X-Plane's global airport file and yields each airport's name, elevation, metadata, land runways and frequencies.
`kuukou/fake-server` serves the `xplane-airports` folder (`apt.dat` only) and reports it in the server check.

`project`: builds an app's `project.json` (version, changes, roadmap, features) from its `CHANGELOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and README `## Features`, with `buildProjectJson`, the three parsers and a Vite plugin that also defines `__PROJECT_VERSION__` (the package.json version) for the app.

fixed: `xplane/cifp`, `faa/cifp`: approach names in the dash form (such as `R18-Z`) give their runway and variant.

added: `faa/airspace`: `parseRestrictiveAirspace` reads restricted, prohibited and other special-use areas from ARINC 424-18 records, in the same shape as `xplane/airspace`.

`xplane/cifp`, `faa/cifp`: leg geometry for curved and navaid-referenced legs: turn direction, recommended navaid with theta and rho, RF arc centre and radius, route distance or hold time, vertical angle.
fixed: `xplane/cifp`: the centre fix column is read as an arc centre only on RF legs.

added: `geo/magnetic`: `declination` gives the magnetic variation from the World Magnetic Model 2025.
`wx/upstream`: `relayWx`, the airport-weather relay's upstream, forwarding only the ident.
`kuukou/fake-server`: a stand-in Kuukou server for apps' tests, with folder manifests and files with Range.
`xplane/fix`, `xplane/nav`: readers for X-Plane's fix and navaid files.
`xplane/awy`: `parseAwySegments` and `airwayRuns`, which stitches segments into airways.
`xplane/hold`, `xplane/msa`, `xplane/mora`: readers for holds, minimum sector altitudes and the grid MORA, with `moraAt`.
`fms`: `writeFms` takes an optional altitude per leg.
`xplane/airspace`: `parseAirspaces` and `airspacesAt` for X-Plane's airspace file.
`xplane/atc`: `parseAtc` and `controllersAt` for X-Plane's ATC file.
`xplane/aptmeta`: `parseAptMeta` reads each airport's own transition altitude and level, elevation, use and longest runway.
`xplane/cifp`, `faa/cifp`: glide slope and glide slope intercept altitudes on legs.
changed: `xplane/cifp`, `faa/cifp`: courses written in whole degrees true are read instead of dropped; legs gain `courseTrue`.

fixed: `xplane/cifp`, `faa/cifp`: below-sea-level leg altitudes are kept instead of dropped.
`faa/cifp`: the transition altitude comes from the airport record, so airports with runways but no procedures get one too.

added: `gfs/fields`, `gfs/grib2`, `gfs/noaa-index`, `gfs/fake-gfs`: winds aloft from NOAA GFS and a stand-in server for tests.
`atmosphere`, `geo`, `geo/track`, `geo/polygon`: ISA atmosphere and great-circle, track and polygon helpers.
`fms`: `parseFms` and `writeFms` for X-Plane's `.fms` flight plan, including the approach.
`xplane/read`: reading X-Plane 12's web API with reconnects.
`xplane/cifp`, `faa/cifp`: procedure readers for X-Plane's and the FAA's files, in one shape.
fixed: `fms`: `writeFms` writes the destination runway for an approach without a STAR block.

now: Every project publishes its version, changes, roadmap and features as `project.json`, read by the hub dashboard.
next: A shared runway matcher for the apps, so a procedure, a plan and the sim agree on which runway is meant.
Minimum sector altitudes from the FAA's procedure file, for apps without the user's X-Plane data.
later: Reading navigation data from a user's own licensed database, kept on their device.
notPlanned: Shipping any navigation data with the package.

features.detail: `xplane/cifp`, `xplane/aptmeta`, `xplane/airspace`, `xplane/atc`, `xplane/fix`, `xplane/nav`, `xplane/awy`, `xplane/hold`, `xplane/msa` and `xplane/mora` parse the files from a user's own X-Plane folder into plain objects.

features.summary: Reads the FAA's procedure and airspace data.
features.detail: `faa/cifp` and `faa/airspace` give SIDs, STARs, approaches, runways and restrictive airspace in the same shape as the X-Plane readers.

features.summary: Reads and writes X-Plane flight plans.
features.detail: `fms` parses and writes the v1100 `.fms` format, approach included.
`geo`, `geo/track`, `geo/polygon` and `geo/magnetic` cover distance, bearing, tracks, polygon tests and the World Magnetic Model.
`gfs/*` decodes NOAA GFS winds, `atmosphere` converts altitude and speed, and `wx/upstream` relays airport weather and weather hazards.
`kuukou/fake-server` and `gfs/fake-gfs` let an app test against made-up servers.
`xplane/read` subscribes to datarefs over the web API and reconnects by itself.
`style/tokens.css`, `style/fonts.css` and `style/base.css` give every Kyoten Kūkō surface the same airside-sign palette, B612 type and Mincho names, light and dark, with the fonts self-hosted.
`family-bar` is a row of airfield taxiway signs along the top of every surface: where you are, and the way to the other apps.

`arinc424/records` names every common record kind and says which columns identify a record, which renumber and which count continuations; `arinc424/codes` puts altitude and speed limits, leg types, route types and turn directions into plain words.
`project` turns a changelog, roadmap and features list into the file the hub dashboard reads.
